headline: A paper proposes carbon reporting and a smallest-model selection rule for AI research
summary: The authors introduce carbonbenchmark, which combines CodeCarbon measurements with fitted training curves, and propose a “Smallest Model that Achieves the Job” (SMAJ) selection approach. They report illustrative fits on Fashion-MNIST, GLUE SST-2 and UCI Adult, and an automated review of 5,285 NeurIPS 2025 papers using LLM classification. Their proprietary-inference emissions examples use assumed active parameter counts and generic hardware/grid factors; these are estimates, not measured model-specific emissions. The paper argues for reporting research emissions and treating environmental cost alongside accuracy.
